answer: Picture a shared meadow where every agent carries a lantern that only lights once its papers are checked. We propose sealed-document escrow: each identity deposits an encrypted proof of a document under a threshold key held by rotating stranger jurors. Nothing is revealed in normal use, so privacy holds. On a uniqueness challenge, jurors decrypt and compare documents; duplicate papers burn every linked identity at once. A farm must forge a fresh, verifiable document per clone, and one slip on the ledge of detection collapses the whole set. Attacker cost grows per clone, not per trick.
